description: We are passionate about space technology, IoT, and Earth science. For this challenge (Be An Earth System Trend Detective!), we are developing a citizen science network combining low-cost physical hardware (ESP32 + environmental sensors) with NASA Earth observation data and AI. Our platform allows users to flash firmware directly from the browser, validate satellite trends, and receive actionable local climate alerts in real time.
summary: OrbitStreet turns anyone into an Earth System Trend Detective. Pick any point on an interactive 3-D globe, choose an environmental variable, and OrbitStreet answers the four detective questions — what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant — using 45 years of real NASA POWER data (MERRA-2 reanalysis). All statistics are computed deterministically in code: Mann-Kendall with tie and Hamed-Rao autocorrelation corrections, Sen's slope with a classic non-parametric 95% confidence interval, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for multi-region comparisons, and a Monte Carlo-validated formula for how many years a local sensor would need to confirm a trend. The engine is verified digit-by-digit against independent references (pymannkendall and SciPy), and an LLM only narrates numbers already calculated — never computes them. A browser-flashable ESP32 ground-truth node extends the tool to citizen science: it measures your street, stores NASA's monthly normals offline, and sends token-signed telemetry. Bilingual (English/Spanish), honest about limitations, with reproducible scientific dossiers.
details:
OrbitStreet is a bilingual (EN/ES) citizen-science web platform that answers NASA's challenge end-to-end: it lets anyone select environmental variables, obtain data for any region, build historical time series, visualize changes over time, and determine trend magnitude and statistical significance.

HOW IT WORKS

The user picks a point on an interactive orthographic globe (d3-geo), selects a variable (mean/max/min temperature, humidity, rainfall, days above 35 °C) and a time window. The server fetches daily NASA POWER (MERRA-2) data since 1981 (cached in PostgreSQL), aggregates it into annual series using strict coverage rules (incomplete or low-coverage years are excluded), and runs a deterministic statistical engine: Mann-Kendall test with tie correction and Hamed-Rao autocorrelation correction, Sen's slope with the classic Sen (1968)/Gilbert (1987) 95% confidence interval, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction when two regions are compared simultaneously. It also computes how many years a local sensor would need to confirm the detected trend (closed-form power formula, Monte Carlo-validated).

Scientific integrity is the core differentiator: the engine is unit-tested digit-by-digit against independent references (pymannkendall 1.4.2 and SciPy theilslopes) on both synthetic and real NASA data (scripts in the repo); incomplete years, reanalysis caveats and the 0.5° grid (~50 km) are declared in the UI; community observations are never mixed with NASA data without provenance labels; and an LLM (Gemini) is only allowed to narrate results that code already computed — it never produces a number. Every analysis can be exported as a reproducible "scientific dossier" (print-ready PDF via a shareable URL that deterministically recomputes the same result server-side) including exact source, method, confidence intervals, independent-validation statement and limitations.

OPEN HARDWARE LAYER

A ~$5 ESP32 node completes the citizen-science loop: flashable directly from the browser (Web Serial + ESP Web Tools, no toolchain), it serves its own offline dashboard from flash memory, reads DHT11/DHT22/BME280/NTC sensors, stores NASA's monthly normals locally to compute ΔT against a historical reference, and sends token-signed telemetry (SHA-256-hashed tokens, batch-rate-limited, reconnect buffer, NTP-stamped) to the platform. Everything is wired via an interactive animated diagram inside the "My station" screen.

TECHNOLOGY

Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, next-intl (EN/ES 1:1 parity), PostgreSQL + Prisma, d3-geo + world-atlas (globe), Recharts, motion, PlatformIO (C++/Arduino core for ESP32), LittleFS, ESPAsyncWebServer, Web Serial/ESP Web Tools, Google Gemini API (narration only), Docker multi-stage build, deployed on Railway with /api/health. Apache-2.0 licensed.

IMPACT

It converts climate-curious citizens into contributors with certified, auditable science: not only can they detect significant trends with honest statistics, they can add street-level ground truth with open hardware — and a documented real case study (Paraguay heat) shows the tool reporting an honest "no significant trend" where the data says so.
